analyses.what_happens: How I read the trace: a flop or assertion at a rising edge in step k uses the values from step k-1. i_clk_mst rises at steps 2,5,7,10,12,14,16,18. i_clk_slv rises at 3,5,7,9,11 and then stops. Edge 2 samples a Setup (step 1: psel=1, penable=0), so the mst FSM goes IDLE->WAIT and reg_req toggles. Through edge 14 the requester keeps psel=penable=1 at every sampled mst edge, as ENV-04 requires. The request crosses: slv edges 3 and 5 fill the synchronizer, edge 7 is SETUP (o_apb_psel=1), edge 9 is ACCESS (o_apb_penable=1 at steps 9-10), and edge 11 samples i_apb_pready=1 (step 10), so the transfer completes and reg_ack toggles. Then i_rst_n_slv alone pulses low at step 15 and is back high at step 16. i_rst_n_mst stays 1 and i_clk_slv has no rising edge in that window. The ack had already reached the mst synchronizer (edges 12 and 14), so mst edge 16 enters RESP and o_apb_pready=1 at steps 16-17. Because the env helper saw i_rst_n_slv=0 at edge 16, it cleared r_env_mst_busy and the requester was free to drop the Access. At step 17 the requester drives psel=1, penable=0 (a new Setup). Mst edge 18 samples step 17: both resets 1, o_apb_pready=1, psel=1, penable=0, so a_CHK_003 fails.
analyses.spec_says: REQ-RESET-002, spec/AsyncAPBBridge_Design_Specification.md:149: "The two resets shall be asserted together and each shall be released synchronously to the clock of its domain, outside the IP. A transfer in flight when a reset is asserted is lost. Asserting only one reset is not supported." (rules AB2-3-39/40/41). Port table :251, i_rst_n_slv: "release synchronous to i_clk_slv outside the IP ... asserted together with i_rst_n_mst". :344: "The two resets are asserted together ... The stopped-clock, warm-reset and retention cases are not supported." :292 lists "One reset asserted alone" as an unsupported condition. What is checked, REQ-FUNC-004 :132: "PREADY ... shall then be high for exactly one cycle of i_clk_mst, in a cycle in which PSEL and PENABLE are high."
analyses.rtl_does: rtl/m_vlsit_apbcdc_mst.sv:165-168: WAIT goes to RESP on w_ack_event = (w_ack_s == reg_req) (:137). :215 sets reg_pready <= w_load_resp. The mst flops reset only on i_rst_n_mst (:199-217), and u_sync_ack is reset only by i_rst_n_mst (:268-277). A reset of the slv domain alone therefore does not cancel an ack that has already reached the mst synchronizer. The mst side still completes the old transfer, which matches the spec's choice to support only resets asserted together (:149).
analyses.checker_does: nnc_chk_mstif.sv:77: assert @(posedge i_clk_mst) disable iff (!i_rst_n_mst) (i_rst_n_slv && o_apb_pready) |-> (i_apb_psel && i_apb_penable). This matches the contract behaviour and REQ-FUNC-004 for a legal requester. The env helper nnc_env.sv:63-72 clears r_env_mst_busy when !i_rst_n_slv is sampled, which lifts ENV-04 (:108-110). ENV-02 (:95-97), 'slv asserted -> mst asserted', is sampled only at posedge i_clk_slv and only when the previous sampled value was 1. Since i_clk_slv has no edge after step 12, the slv-only pulse at step 15 is never seen.

candidates.evidence_for: The failure needs i_rst_n_slv to be asserted alone (step 15, i_rst_n_mst=1) and released without any i_clk_slv rising edge (step 16). Both break REQ-RESET-002 (spec:149, AB2-3-39/40/41: asserted together, release synchronous to own clock, 'Asserting only one reset is not supported'). They also break the stopped-clock exclusion (spec:344). ENV-01/ENV-02 (nnc_env.sv:90-97) only sample the resets at their own clock edge, so a reset pulse between edges or on a stopped clock escapes them. That same unseen reset clears r_env_mst_busy (nnc_env.sv:64-65) and lets the requester abandon the Access phase before PREADY.
candidates.evidence_against: None in the spec. The DUT behaviour after a single-domain reset is explicitly unsupported.

candidates.evidence_for: o_apb_pready=1 is sampled together with a Setup cycle, which on its face breaks REQ-FUNC-004.
candidates.evidence_against: This only happens after a reset of one domain alone, which spec:149 and :292 declare unsupported. Under legal reset sequencing i_rst_n_mst would be asserted at the same time and clear the FSM, reg_pready and u_sync_ack (mst.sv:199-217, 268-277).

candidates.evidence_for: The disable iff contains only !i_rst_n_mst, and i_rst_n_slv appears only in the antecedent (nnc_chk_mstif.sv:77). The contract (contract.json:1407) and spec:652 say assertions are disabled while either reset is asserted.
candidates.evidence_against: For this single-cycle |-> property the antecedent term has the same effect as a disable. At the failing edge (step-17 values) both resets are 1, so adding !i_rst_n_slv to disable iff would not remove this counterexample.

analyses.options: (1) Add environment assumptions, evaluated on the formal global clock rather than on the DUT clocks, that state REQ-RESET-002 (spec:149, AB2-3-39/40/41). (a) Asserted together: assume property (@($global_clock) $fell(i_rst_n_mst) |-> !i_rst_n_slv) and assume property (@($global_clock) $fell(i_rst_n_slv) |-> !i_rst_n_mst). (b) Release synchronous to the own clock: assume property (@($global_clock) $rose(i_rst_n_mst) |-> $rose(i_clk_mst)) and the same for slv. These replace or strengthen ENV-01/ENV-02 (nnc_env.sv:90-97), which miss resets between edges. (2) Optionally, based on spec:233/250 ('free running') and :344 ('stopped-clock ... not supported'), add a bounded clock-liveness assumption so that each clock rises at least every K global steps. Then re-run. If CHK-003 still fails under legal reset sequencing, look at mst.sv:165-168/215 as a real RTL issue. Do not weaken CHK-003.

analyses.what_happens: i_clk_mst rises at 2,4,8,12,14,16,18. i_clk_slv rises at 3,5,7,9,11 and then stops. Edge 2 samples a Setup (step 1), so a request is launched. The requester holds psel=penable=1 at mst edges 4, 8 and 12. On the slv side, SETUP comes at edge 7, ACCESS at edge 9 (o_apb_penable=1 at steps 9-10), and completion at edge 11 (i_apb_pready=1 at step 10), so reg_ack toggles. The ack reaches the mst synchronizer at edges 12 and 14. Then i_rst_n_slv alone goes low at steps 13-15 and comes back high at step 16. i_rst_n_mst stays 1 and there is no i_clk_slv edge. Mst edge 16 enters RESP and o_apb_pready=1 at steps 16-17. The env saw !i_rst_n_slv at edges 14 and 16, so it cleared busy, and the checker cleared chk006_armed (nnc_chk_mstif.sv:66). At step 17 the requester drives a new Setup (psel=1, penable=0). Mst edge 18 samples step 17: o_apb_pready=1 with chk006_armed=0, so a_CHK_006 fails. In the same cycle there is a Setup with o_apb_pready=1, so a_CHK_006_b also fails.
analyses.spec_says: REQ-RESET-002 spec:149: "The two resets shall be asserted together and each shall be released synchronously to the clock of its domain ... Asserting only one reset is not supported." The same requirement appears at spec:251 and :344 ("The stopped-clock ... cases are not supported") and at :292. What is checked, REQ-FUNC-004 spec:132: "PREADY ... shall be low from the Setup phase until the response is available, and shall then be high for exactly one cycle". Also spec:213: "PREADY of the requester side is high only in state RESP, one cycle per transfer."
analyses.rtl_does: rtl/m_vlsit_apbcdc_mst.sv:137 and :165-168: WAIT->RESP when the synchronized ack equals reg_req. :215 sets reg_pready. The whole mst domain, including u_sync_ack (:268-277), is reset only by i_rst_n_mst. The slv-only reset at steps 13-15 clears reg_ack in slv (slv.sv:198-199), but the toggle had already been captured by the mst synchronizer at edges 12 and 14. The mst side therefore finishes the transfer that was in flight.
analyses.checker_does: nnc_chk_mstif.sv:65-69: chk006_armed is cleared when either reset is low or o_apb_pready=1, and set on a Setup. :92: (i_rst_n_slv && o_apb_pready) |-> chk006_armed. :94: (i_rst_n_slv && psel && !penable) |-> (!o_apb_pready ##1 !o_apb_pready). Both have disable iff (!i_rst_n_mst). By clearing armed on !i_rst_n_slv, the checker treats the slv-only reset as ending the transfer. The RTL mst side does not do that.

candidates.evidence_for: The counterexample needs a reset of the slv domain alone (steps 13-15, i_rst_n_mst=1), released at step 16 with no i_clk_slv edge. Both are forbidden by REQ-RESET-002 (spec:149, AB2-3-39/40/41) and :344. ENV-02 (nnc_env.sv:95-97) samples only at posedge i_clk_slv, and that clock has no edge after step 11, so the pulse is invisible to the environment. The same pulse cleared r_env_mst_busy (nnc_env.sv:64-65), which allowed the early new Setup at step 17.
candidates.evidence_against: None. The spec does not define behaviour for a single-domain reset.

candidates.evidence_for: A PREADY appears with no Setup since the last reset, and it coincides with a Setup cycle.
candidates.evidence_against: This only happens after an unsupported single reset (spec:149, :292). With both resets asserted together, mst.sv:199-217 would return the FSM to IDLE and clear reg_pready and u_sync_ack.

candidates.evidence_for: The checker's helper (nnc_chk_mstif.sv:66) disarms on !i_rst_n_slv, assuming a slv reset also aborts the mst transfer. That assumption only holds if the resets are asserted together.
candidates.evidence_against: That is exactly the spec's assumption (spec:149). The contract behaviour (contract.json:485) is implemented faithfully for legal resets.

analyses.options: (1) Add global-clock environment assumptions for REQ-RESET-002 (AB2-3-39/40/41, spec:149): (a) a falling edge of either reset implies the other reset is low in the same step; (b) $rose(i_rst_n_mst) only together with $rose(i_clk_mst), and $rose(i_rst_n_slv) only together with $rose(i_clk_slv). (2) Optionally add a clock-liveness bound supported by spec:233/250/344. Re-run CHK-006. A counterexample under these assumptions would point to mst.sv:165-168/215. Do not drop the reset clearing of chk006_armed or relax CHK-006.

analyses.what_happens: i_clk_mst rises only at step 2 and is stopped afterwards. i_clk_slv rises at 3,5,7,9,11. Mst edge 2 samples a Setup (step 1), so reg_req=1. Then i_rst_n_mst alone falls at step 3 while i_rst_n_slv=1. It is released at step 5 and again at step 8, both times with no i_clk_mst edge, and is low again at steps 7 and 9-12. The request bit reached u_sync_req before the mst reset (slv edges 3 and 5), so slv edge 7 enters SETUP (o_apb_psel=1, o_apb_penable=0 at steps 7-8). Slv edge 9 samples step 8: both resets 1, psel=1, penable=0, so the antecedent holds. At step 9, i_rst_n_slv drops asynchronously and clears o_apb_psel. It is released at step 10 with no i_clk_slv edge (the next edge is step 11). Slv edge 11 samples step 10: i_rst_n_slv=1 (so not disabled), o_apb_psel=0, o_apb_penable=0. The |=> consequent fails.
analyses.spec_says: REQ-RESET-002 spec:149: "The two resets shall be asserted together and each shall be released synchronously to the clock of its domain ... Asserting only one reset is not supported." Spec:234/251: release synchronous to i_clk_mst / i_clk_slv. Spec:341-342: deassertion "Synchronous to i_clk_mst" / "Synchronous to i_clk_slv". Spec:344: "stopped-clock ... cases are not supported". Spec:652: assertions "are disabled while either reset is asserted, except SVA-016." What is checked, REQ-FUNC-008 spec:136 (PENABLE "high from the next cycle") and spec:202 ("raises PSEL (Setup), and one cycle later PENABLE (Access)").
analyses.rtl_does: rtl/m_vlsit_apbcdc_slv.sv:162: SETUP always goes to ACCESS. :205-206: psel and penable are decoded from the next state. So without a reset the Setup lasts exactly one cycle. :197-202: the asynchronous reset on i_rst_n_slv clears reg_apb_psel and reg_apb_penable, as REQ-RESET-001 (spec:148) requires. The failure is purely this asynchronous clear at step 9.
analyses.checker_does: nnc_chk_slvif.sv:74: @(posedge i_clk_slv) disable iff (!i_rst_n_slv) (i_rst_n_mst && o_apb_psel && !o_apb_penable) |=> (o_apb_psel && o_apb_penable). i_rst_n_mst appears only in the antecedent and is not in disable iff. In this formal run, disable iff was in effect evaluated at the sampled slv edges (steps 8 and 10), both with i_rst_n_slv=1, so the reset pulse at step 9 did not disable the attempt. At the consequent edge, i_rst_n_mst is 0 (step 10), but that does not disable the check.

candidates.evidence_for: The trace breaks REQ-RESET-002 three ways. (1) i_rst_n_mst is asserted alone at step 3 and at step 7 (spec:149 'Asserting only one reset is not supported'; ENV-01 nnc_env.sv:90-92 samples only at posedge i_clk_mst, which never rises again after step 2). (2) i_rst_n_mst is released at steps 5 and 8, and i_rst_n_slv at step 10, without any edge of their own clock (spec:149, :341-342). (3) i_clk_mst is stopped (spec:233, :344). If release were synchronous to i_clk_slv, the earliest release would be at the step-11 edge, which samples i_rst_n_slv=0, so the attempt would be disabled. If resets were asserted together, the step-3 reset would also clear u_sync_req and o_apb_psel would never rise.

contract.json:1407 and spec:652 say assertions are disabled while either reset is asserted. The checker puts i_rst_n_mst only in the antecedent (nnc_chk_slvif.sv:74), so a mst reset seen at the consequent edge (step 10, i_rst_n_mst=0) does not disable the |=> attempt. With disable iff (!i_rst_n_slv || !i_rst_n_mst), this trace would be disabled at edge 11.
candidates.evidence_against: Fixing the checker alone leaves the illegal reset sequences in the formal state space, and other checks (CHK-017, CHK-003) still fail from them. The slv-reset pulse itself (step 9) is already in disable iff. It is missed only because it is asserted and released between sample points, which a legal environment does not allow.

candidates.evidence_for: o_apb_psel falls after a single Setup cycle without an Access phase.
candidates.evidence_against: This is caused by the asynchronous reset at step 9, which REQ-RESET-001 (spec:148) requires. slv.sv:162 always goes SETUP->ACCESS.

analyses.options: (1) Add environment assumptions for REQ-RESET-002 (spec:149, AB2-3-39/40/41), clocked by the formal global clock: resets asserted in the same step, and each release only at a rising edge of its own clock ($rose(i_rst_n_slv) |-> $rose(i_clk_slv), same for mst). These replace the clock-sampled ENV-01/ENV-02 (nnc_env.sv:90-97). Optionally add a clock-liveness bound (spec:233/250/344). (2) Separately, to match contract.json:1407 and spec:652, make the checker's disable iff (!i_rst_n_slv || !i_rst_n_mst) instead of carrying i_rst_n_mst only in the antecedent. This is a consistency fix the spec supports, not a weakening. Re-run. A remaining counterexample under legal resets would point to slv.sv:162/205-206.

analyses.what_happens: i_clk_mst rises only at step 2. i_clk_slv rises at 3,5,7,9,11,13. Mst edge 2 launches a request from the Setup at step 1. i_rst_n_mst alone falls at step 3 (i_rst_n_slv=1) and is released at step 7 with no mst clock edge. It falls again at step 9, is released at step 10 with no edge, and falls at step 11. The request bit was already in u_sync_req, so slv edge 7 is SETUP (o_apb_psel=1) and edge 9 is ACCESS (o_apb_penable=1 at steps 9-10). Slv edge 11 samples step 10: both resets 1, psel=penable=1, i_apb_pready=0, so the antecedent holds. At step 11, i_rst_n_slv (with i_rst_n_mst) is asserted and clears o_apb_psel and o_apb_penable. It is released at step 12 with no i_clk_slv edge. Slv edge 13 samples step 12: i_rst_n_slv=1, o_apb_psel=0, so the consequent fails.
analyses.spec_says: REQ-RESET-002 spec:149: "The two resets shall be asserted together and each shall be released synchronously to the clock of its domain ... Asserting only one reset is not supported." Spec:341-342: deassertion synchronous to the own clock. Spec:344: stopped-clock not supported. Spec:652: assertions disabled while either reset is asserted. What is checked: spec:203 "The slv FSM waits in ACCESS until the completer drives PREADY", and REQ-FUNC-005 (rules AB2-3-10): "The bridge shall wait without limit (no timeout, DEC-006)."
analyses.rtl_does: rtl/m_vlsit_apbcdc_slv.sv:163-166: ACCESS is left only when i_apb_pready=1. :205-206 keep psel=penable=1 while in ACCESS. There is no timeout path. The only way out without PREADY is the asynchronous reset at :197-202, which is required by REQ-RESET-001 (spec:148). That is what happens at step 11.
analyses.checker_does: nnc_chk_slvif.sv:79: disable iff (!i_rst_n_slv) (i_rst_n_mst && o_apb_psel && o_apb_penable && !i_apb_pready) |=> (o_apb_psel && o_apb_penable). The reset pulse at step 11 lies between the sampled points (steps 10 and 12), and both have i_rst_n_slv=1, so the attempt is not disabled. i_rst_n_mst is 0 at the consequent sample (step 12) but is not in disable iff.

candidates.evidence_for: Illegal reset sequencing. (1) i_rst_n_mst is asserted alone at step 3 (spec:149). ENV-01 (nnc_env.sv:90-92) cannot see it because i_clk_mst never rises after step 2. (2) Releases at steps 7, 10 (mst) and 12 (slv) happen without an edge of their own clock (spec:149, :341-342). (3) i_clk_mst is stopped (spec:233, :344). With release synchronous to i_clk_slv, the slv edge right after the step-11 assertion would sample i_rst_n_slv=0 and disable the attempt. With resets asserted together at step 3, the request would never cross.

i_rst_n_mst is only in the antecedent (nnc_chk_slvif.sv:79), not in disable iff, which differs from contract.json:1407 and spec:652. At the consequent edge (step-12 values) i_rst_n_mst=0, so with disable iff (!i_rst_n_slv || !i_rst_n_mst) this trace would be disabled.
candidates.evidence_against: The illegal sequence would remain reachable for other checks. The slv reset pulse is already in disable iff and is missed only because of the illegal asynchronous release.

candidates.evidence_for: The Access phase ends without i_apb_pready.
candidates.evidence_against: It ends because of the reset at step 11, which REQ-RESET-001 (spec:148) requires. slv.sv:163-166 has no timeout.

analyses.options: (1) Add global-clock environment assumptions for REQ-RESET-002 (spec:149, AB2-3-39/40/41): assertion of either reset implies the other is asserted in the same step, and each reset rises only with a rising edge of its own clock. Optionally add a clock-liveness bound (spec:233/250/344). (2) Align the checker with contract.json:1407 and spec:652 by using disable iff (!i_rst_n_slv || !i_rst_n_mst). Mst edge 2 samples a write Setup (step 1: psel=1, penable=0, pwrite=1), so the payload has pwrite=1 and reg_req toggles. The request crosses (slv edges 3 and 5), and slv edge 7 loads reg_apb_payload: o_apb_psel=1 and o_apb_pwrite=1 at steps 7-8. i_rst_n_mst alone falls at step 7 (i_rst_n_slv=1) and is released at step 8 with no mst clock edge. Slv edge 9 samples step 8: both resets 1, psel=1, penable=0, so the antecedent holds. At step 9 both resets are asserted. Spec:652: assertions disabled while either reset is asserted. analyses.rtl_does: rtl/m_vlsit_apbcdc_slv.sv:215-220: reg_apb_payload is loaded only on w_load_req (IDLE & request event, :138) and is otherwise held. Its asynchronous reset to 0 on i_rst_n_slv (:216-217) is the only cause of the change at step 9. The reset clear is required by spec:148.

The step-9 reset pulse falls between the sampled points (steps 8 and 10), so the attempt is not disabled. i_rst_n_mst=0 at the consequent sample (step 10) but is only in the antecedent.

candidates.evidence_for: (1) i_rst_n_mst is asserted alone at step 7 (spec:149). It is invisible to ENV-01 (nnc_env.sv:90-92) because i_clk_mst is stopped after step 2. (2) i_rst_n_mst is released at step 8 and i_rst_n_slv at step 10, with no edge of their own clock (spec:149, :341-342). (3) i_clk_mst is stopped (spec:233, :344). With i_rst_n_slv released only at a slv rising edge, the slv edge after the step-9 assertion samples i_rst_n_slv=0 and the attempt is disabled.
Per contract.json:1407 and spec:652, the check should be disabled while either reset is asserted. i_rst_n_mst is not in disable iff (nnc_chk_slvif.sv:89), and at the consequent sample i_rst_n_mst=0.
candidates.evidence_against: This alone would not remove the illegal reset patterns that also cause CHK-017/CHK-003/CHK-006. The field change is a required reset effect, not a stability violation within a transfer.

candidates.evidence_for: o_apb_pwrite changes while a transfer is shown as active at the antecedent.
candidates.evidence_against: The change comes from the asynchronous reset required by REQ-RESET-001 (spec:148). Otherwise reg_apb_payload loads only in IDLE (slv.sv:138, 218-219).

analyses.what_happens: i_clk_mst rises at steps 2 and 5, then stops. i_clk_slv rises at 3,5,7,9,11. Mst edge 2 samples a read Setup with i_apb_pwdata=3 (step 1), so the payload has pwdata=3 and reg_req toggles. Mst edge 5 samples step 4 (psel=penable=1, so ENV-04 holds). The request crosses at slv edges 3 and 5. Slv edge 7 enters SETUP and loads the payload: o_apb_psel=1 and o_apb_pwdata=3 at steps 7-8 (a legal Setup entry). At step 9, i_rst_n_slv alone falls (i_rst_n_mst stays 1 until step 10). The asynchronous reset clears o_apb_pwdata to 0 and o_apb_psel to 0. i_rst_n_slv is released at step 10 with no i_clk_slv edge. Slv edge 11 samples step 10: both resets 1, o_apb_pwdata=0, and the previous sampled value (step 8) was 3, so !$stable holds. o_apb_psel=0, so the required (psel && !penable && !$past(psel)) is false and the assertion fails.

Spec:251: i_rst_n_slv is "asserted together with i_rst_n_mst". Spec:342: RST-SLV deassertion "Synchronous to i_clk_slv". Spec:344: stopped clocks not supported. What is checked, REQ-IF-003 spec:140: "Outputs that need not be valid shall hold a stable value (reset value zero)." Spec:202: the slv FSM "loads reg_apb_payload ... raises PSEL (Setup)". Spec:148: payload registers are 0 while reset is asserted.
